correctness.rationale: The length-2 scattered-subsequence signature of a binary half is exactly (K,I) with K the one-count and I its 01 scattered-pair count. The coefficient squared sum of Gaussian binomials is exact. For |k-n/2|<=n^(2/3), Canfield–Janson–Zeilberger Theorem 4.5 supplies the uniform local limit for multiset inversions (the multiplicities are proportional to n, satisfying its uniformity hypotheses). Its Gaussian L2 integral yields (2 sqrt(3)/sqrt(pi))n^(-3/2); Vandermonde and concentration give binomial collision ~1/sqrt(pi n). Multiplication gives S_n/4^n~2 sqrt(3)/(pi n^2). Chebyshev bounds the conditional squared-density tails, binomial Chernoff bounds the k tails. Independent direct 2-deck enumeration agrees n=1..12, including S12=122570. Finite checks do not establish the limit.

evidence: Canfield–Janson–Zeilberger Theorem 4.5 gives a uniform local CLT for Mahonian inversion statistics conditional on symbol counts; it does not perform the independent binomial count mixture.
